quote: All other liability is expressly waived and released as a condition of, and consideration for, the execution of this Agreement by the Servicer or the Marketing Agent, as applicable. Each of the Servicer and the Marketing Agent, severally and not jointly, will be liable only for its own willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under this Agreement.
rationale: The liability architecture sits at or above the fallback on its material terms, so we do not redline it. (1) Mutuality: Section 6.2(a) (Servicer/Marketing Agent, p0283) and Section 5.2(a) (Depositor, p0243) are parallel "liable only for specific obligations" waivers, and our entities have the additional benefit of Section 9.6 limited recourse (p0378, claims against Depositor/Issuer limited to the Depositor Transferred Property) and Section 9.7 (p0381-p0382). Our side's exposure is therefore effectively bounded while the counterparty's is not. (2) Cap basis: there is no monetary or fee-based cap anywhere in the document — searches for "exceed"/aggregate-liability language return no cap, and the Servicing Fee (p0975) is never used as a liability ceiling. The fallback's "12 months of fees" cap exists to floor Vendor exposure; here Cellco's exposure in amount is unlimited, which exceeds the fallback and benefits us, so we do not introduce a cap that would only weaken our position. (3) Carve-outs: because no cap exists, indemnification (Section 6.3, p0291-p0292), confidentiality/data-protection breaches (Exhibit A policies, p0146), gross negligence and willful misconduct all carry unlimited exposure, and gross negligence, bad faith and willful misconduct are the express standards of Servicer liability and indemnity. Minor shortfalls of the preferred wording — no general mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages (the only such bar, p0469, binds the arbitral panel), no USD 1,000,000 floor, and no express "payment obligations are not damages" statement — are noted rather than flagged; the first two are only meaningful alongside a cap, and none is a material failure of the fallback. We note for the record (outside this rule) that Section 6.2(a) limits Cellco's liability to willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, excluding ordinary negligence; that is a standard-of-care point, is mirrored for the Depositor, and is market standard for this securitization structure rather than a cap deviation.

This Agreement will terminate on the earlier to occur of (a) the date upon which the last remaining Receivable is paid in full, settled, sold or written off and any amounts received are applied and (b) the Issuer is terminated under Section 8.1 of the Trust Agreement.
rationale: This transfer and servicing agreement contains no renewal mechanic at all. Searches for "renew", "automatically renew", "successive", "extension/expire", "term of this Agreement" and fee-escalation language return no auto-renewal term, no non-renewal notice window and no price-uplift right; the term simply runs under Section 8.3 (p0363) until the last Receivable is paid in full/settled/sold/written off or the Issuer is terminated under the Trust Agreement. Because renewal is not automatic and no price increase is permitted, each conditional fallback element (60-day non-renewal window; 5% uplift cap) and each conditional preferred element (12-month renewal term, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder, CPI/3% cap) is satisfied vacuously, and any extension of this self-liquidating term could only be effected by the parties amending the Agreement in writing under Section 10.4 (p0392) — i.e. by mutual written agreement, the preferred position. There is nothing here that traps us in a renewal or exposes us to an uncapped uplift, so no redline is warranted; inserting a renewal-and-uplift construct into a securitization structure that terminates on final payment would be inapposite.

rationale: Section 7.5 contains a transition mechanic triggered by the Servicer's resignation or termination (7.5(a) cooperation; 7.5(b) transfer of Receivable Files and records), so the first fallback element is already met. The clause nonetheless fails the fallback on two material terms: there is no minimum transition assistance period (Section 7.3 only requires the Servicer to continue until a Successor Servicer accepts engagement or until the date stated in the termination notice, which may be far shorter than 90 days), and delivery of the Receivable Files and records is governed only by an open-ended "as soon as practicable" standard with no 30-day outside date. We propose the shortest fallback-level cure: a 90-day assistance period and a 30-day backstop for delivery. We have not pursued the preferred machine-readable-format and certified-deletion elements, and we leave the Section 7.5(b) carve-back for processes, models and servicing software untouched (that point sits with the IP rule).
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
sectionRef: § VII SERVICER RESIGNATION AND TERMINATION; SUCCESSOR SERVICER

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 7.5(a): "On its resignation or termination, the Servicer will cooperate with the Issuer, the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee and the Successor Servicer in effecting ... an orderly transition"; 7.5(b) likewise runs from "the effective date of its resignation or termination". Resignation and termination are the only end-of-engagement events for the Servicer under this servicing structure (there is no separate servicer 'expiry' concept), so every covered ending is captured, and the inserted sentence uses the same trigger.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence commits only to "at least ninety (90) days after the effective date of its resignation or termination"; no six-month period appears anywhere in Section 7.5 or 7.3.

elements.evidence: No rate mechanic was added. Retained 7.5(c) runs the other way (transition expenses of the Issuer/trustees/Successor Servicer are "paid by the resigning or terminated Servicer"); there is no then-current-rates pricing for the assistance.

elements.evidence: Inserted: "in any event will deliver the Receivable Files and the accounts and records maintained by the Servicer to the Successor Servicer no later than thirty (30) days after such effective date" — a hard 30-day outside date measured from the effective date of resignation or termination, backstopping the retained "as soon as practicable" standard.

elements.evidence: The insertion is silent on format; retained 7.5(b) only requires delivery of "the Receivable Files and the accounts and records maintained by the Servicer" with no commonly used, machine-readable format requirement.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion or written certification obligation exists in Section 7.5 as rendered; nothing was added.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same retained trigger in 7.5(a)/(b) ("On its resignation or termination" / "after the effective date of its resignation or termination"), and the inserted period is anchored to that identical effective date, so the assistance period applies after every covered ending, not merely an anticipated one.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "The predecessor Servicer will provide the transition assistance described in this Section 7.5 for at least ninety (90) days after the effective date of its resignation or termination." The scope is defined by reference to the cooperation and transfer duties in Section 7.5, so the trigger and content are not undefined. Section 7.3 (performance of servicing until a Successor Servicer accepts, or the date in the termination notice) addresses continued servicing rather than transition assistance and does not contradict the new floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted 30-day outside date for delivery of the Receivable Files and the accounts and records to the Successor Servicer (the transferee engaged by the Issuer under Section 7.4), replacing reliance on the open-ended "as soon as practicable" standard for timing purposes.

verification.notes: Fallback level is complete: the single inserted sentence supplies the two missing fallback terms (a 90-day minimum assistance period and a 30-day outside date for delivery of the Receivable Files and records), while the trigger element was already satisfied by retained Section 7.5(a)/(b). Preferred level is not reached. To reach it the drafter would need to (i) extend assistance to up to six (6) months, (ii) state that assistance is at the Servicer's then-current rates, (iii) require delivery in a commonly used, machine-readable format, and (iv) add a post-return deletion and written certification obligation. The finding correctly does not claim these. Minimality holds: nothing was deleted (the "as soon as practicable" standard, the processes/models/servicing-software carve-back and the 7.5(c) expense allocation all survive), no format, deletion, survival tail, expense or procedural extras were added, and the addition is confined to the two fallback elements actually missing. Intent is preserved: the 30-day date operates as a backstop to the retained "as soon as practicable" duty in 7.5(b)(ii) rather than replacing it, and Section 7.3's continued-performance mechanic is untouched. One drafting watch-point only (not a failure): the phrase "in any event" sits alongside the retained sentence relieving the Servicer of any obligation to provide items "covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment or a confidentiality agreement or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies" — since the primary 7.5(b)(ii) delivery duty already coexists with that carve-back, no new conflict is created, but adding "subject to the last sentence of Section 7.5(b)" would remove any argument of inconsistency. Classification as a deviation is right: without the insertion the clause failed the fallback on two material terms (no minimum assistance period; no outside date for data delivery).

quote: (x) Servicing Procedures. It has complied in all material respects with the Servicing Procedures with respect to the Receivables.
rationale: The Servicer's obligations run to a performance standard (Section 3.2(a): \"with reasonable care using that degree of skill and attention that the Servicer exercises for all comparable device payment plan agreement receivables\") and Section 6.1(a) contains point-in-time reps on compliance with Law and with the Servicing Procedures. There is, however, no conformance warranty for the receivables systems/software or reports the Servicer delivers, no warranty duration, and no repair, replacement or refund remedy — the only remedy machinery is acquisition of affected Receivables, expressly stated as the sole remedy for the narrow Section 3.2(b)-(d) breaches. That fails every fallback element, so we insert the shortest fallback warranty (90 days software conformance to documentation, 30 days services) with repair/replacement or refund. Section 3.3(g)'s sole-remedy language is confined to Section 3.2(b)/(c)/(d) and so does not swallow the new warranty; the new remedy is drafted as a specific Servicer obligation for purposes of Section 6.2(a).

verification.notes: Fallback level is complete: the single inserted "Performance Warranty" paragraph supplies a 90-day software-to-documentation warranty, a 30-day services warranty, and repair/replacement or refund remedies, so the deviation finding and the fallback target are correctly matched. Preferred level fails on four elements: the software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, the services period is 30 days rather than 90 days, there is no professional-and-workmanlike warranty (Section 3.2(a) is a servicing covenant, not a warranty), and there is no no-malicious-code warranty. Minimality holds: one concise insertion for a missing clause, no deletion or paraphrase of existing text, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or extra damages language, and no procedure beyond the remedy itself. Electing party ("at the Issuer's option") is inherent to the remedy formulation rather than an added requirement, though it departs from the model language's Vendor-option formulation and may be a negotiation point. Intent is preserved: Section 3.3(g)'s sole-remedy language is expressly limited to Sections 3.2(b), (c) and (d), so the new remedy is not swallowed and no retained sentence contradicts it; the Section 6.1(a) compliance representations and the acquisition-of-Receivables machinery survive intact. "Servicing Fee" and "Issuer" are defined terms, so no dangling reference is created. If the drafter wants the preferred position, the operative repairs are: change "90 days" to twelve (12) months for software, "30 days" to ninety (90) days for services, add an express professional-and-workmanlike performance warranty, and add a no-malicious-code warranty — the margin comment's offer to discuss 12 months does not itself meet any element.
